2014_071_100714mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education held October 7, 2014 at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The bulk of the packet is the June 2014 Treasurer's Report — a full June YTD fiscal-year-2014 summary revenue and expense report for every fund plus a Pentamation check register whose TOTAL REPORT is $4,580,456.80 — alongside the resignations of Assistant Superintendent for Business Services Mark Rajter and Executive Director of Maintenance & Operations Kenneth Miller. With the treasurer's post vacant, the Board was asked to appoint Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky as temporary Board Treasurer.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, October 7, 2014, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000). Cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition**
Student representatives Dalia Ibrahim (Athens), Avirath Kumar (International Academy-East), Sylvester Hanna (Niles) and Patty Durell (Troy High), with alternates Bobby Hahn and Zari Saynganthone. Sixty-seven National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists and one National Achievement Semifinalist (Noah McNeal) honored by resolution, with a reception October 15th. The new Superintendent's Student Advisory Board drew 55 applications and seated 24 students (6 seniors, 7 juniors, 7 sophomores, 4 freshmen). TSD Mission Moment: Bemis Elementary leadership initiatives, presented by principal Jeremey Whan.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the September 2, 2014 meeting (Resolutions 14-095 through 14-101, each carried Yes 5, No 0 with Hauff and Schmidt absent) and the September 16, 2014 workshop, plus the June 2014 Treasurer's Report.

**Personnel**
Resignations accepted from Kenneth Miller, Executive Director of Maintenance & Operations (hired April 1, 2002, effective October 6, 2014) and Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services (hired July 1, 2010, effective September 26, 2014). New probationary hires: Meredith Adkins (.5 FTE speech language pathologist), Taylor Firman (1.0 FTE social studies), Rebecca Johnson (.4 FTE social studies) and Holly White (.8 FTE mathematics). Jasen Witt reported teacher evaluations of 574 Highly Effective, 201 Effective, 9 Minimally Effective and 2 Ineffective, and total Performance-Based Compensation paid of $461,371.83.

**Curriculum**
Sex Education Advisory Board membership for 2014/2015 co-chaired by Amy Buchanan and Nicole Jenkins; professional development plan presented by Anne Mull; Advanced Placement report by Mark Dziatczak (170 AP Scholars, 90 with Honor, 252 with Distinction, 76 National AP Scholars).

**Business**
Food service wireless temperature monitoring awarded to SMART Temp, LLC for $38,504.00 from the 2014-2015 Food Services Fund (Bid 9796). Athens High School masonry re-bid awarded to Efficient Design, Inc. for $73,482.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Dr. Richard Machesky appointed temporary Board Treasurer until an Assistant Superintendent of Business Services is appointed.

**Meeting.** The Troy School District Board of Education met in regular session at 7:00 PM on October 7, 2014 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices are at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition.** Student representatives: Dalia Ibrahim (Athens High School), Avirath "Avi" Kumar (International Academy-East), Sylvester Hanna (Niles Community High School) and Patty Durell (Troy High School, whose Relay for Life team raised over $25,000 in three years), with alternates Bobby Hahn and Zari Saynganthone. A resolution dated the seventh day of October, 2014 honored one National Achievement Scholarship Semifinalist, Noah McNeal, and sixty-seven National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, with copies presented at an October 15th reception; qualification requires a score in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT. The new Superintendent's Student Advisory Board received 55 applications and selected 24 students — 6 seniors, 7 juniors, 7 sophomores, 4 freshmen. The Mission Moment featured Bemis Elementary principal Jeremey Whan and teacher Mary Tovey.

**Minutes.** At the September 2, 2014 meeting, President Nancy Philippart presided with Edmunds, Fleming, Miletti and Underwood present, Hauff and Schmidt absent, and approximately 60 audience members. The Michigan Association of School Boards cited the Board's Honor Board achievement and Standard of Excellence Award, Nancy Philippart's Master Board Member and Advocacy Skill Specialty Awards, and Karl Schmidt's Level One Certification and Award of Merit; ASBO International awarded a Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the CAFR for the year ended June 30, 2013. Boulan Park Middle School's LINKS program collected 1,022 personal letters, 2,790 items and $142 in cash for troops in Afghanistan. Resolution 14-095 approved August 5, 2014 minutes; 14-096 approved 26 new hires; 14-097 gave Dan House a two-year probationary administrative contract as Assistant Principal, Troy High School as of September 3, 2014; 14-098 approved Troy High School addition and remodeling bids totaling $2,629,095.00; 14-099 approved Boulan Park and Larson Middle School bids totaling $3,425,240.00; 14-100 approved science supplies and equipment totaling $69,609.52; 14-101 amended and forwarded the 2015 Tax Rate Request Form L-4029. All carried Yes 5, No 0, Hauff and Schmidt absent. Mr. Witt reported 44 new teachers hired, eight of them TSD graduates and 27 with education beyond a bachelor's degree; summer programming drew over 3,200 registrants and 125 TSD staff; enrollment came in under the lowest projection by Fred Ignatovich. The meeting adjourned at 9:03 p.m. The September 16 workshop, attended by all seven members plus Jim Crowley of Clark Hill and Ron Curtis and Doug Babby of Barton Malow, covered operating mill renewal, bond projects, iPad rollout and superintendent goals, adjourning at 10:50 p.m.

**Treasurer's Report, June 2014.** Certified by Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, in a memo dated October 2, 2014. Debt funds zero; Building & Site Funds (404, 499) 2,421,785.44; Internal Service zero; Student Activity (700, 701) 445,283.04; Memorial Scholarship (750) 27,863.44; Total Other Funds $2,894,931.92. TOTAL CHECK DISBURSEMENTS $4,580,456.80. The recap adds ACH debits $22,000.90, outgoing wire transfers $2,696,267.18, P-Card purchases $166,845.76 and prior period void disbursements $(3,723.00) for TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS IN PERIOD $7,461,847.64. The ACH/P-Card detail listing prints a grand total of $188,846.66.

Total instruction was 88,155,963 budgeted against 90,478,889 actual, total support services 43,014,356 against 42,680,856, and total expenditures $131,326,219 against $133,266,489. **Wire transfers and check register.** The main June wire listing totals -$2,356,318.06 and includes MPSERS UAAL June 14 $311,004.33, MPSERS DB 5/23/14 pay $896,163.33, payroll transfers of $2,298,302.54 and $1,653,522.15, payroll taxes of $1,099,939.61, MPSERS 6/6/14 pay $1,212,689.14 and a VRIP payment of $84,336.49; a supplemental listing totals $339,949.12 and includes a BCBSM July premium of $151,980.65 and an MPSERS UAAL rate stabilization payment of $320,973.20. The Pentamation ACCTPA21 check register dated 07/24/2014, accounting period 1/15, covers checks 14005807-14006618 issued 06/03, 06/04, 06/10, 06/18 and 06/25/14, all cash account A1003 with sales tax 0.00, and prints TOTAL REPORT $4,580,456.80. Fund totals: 101 1,179,298.08; 120 192.00; 122 336,370.53; 414 2014 Cap Proj-Series 1 2,421,236.19; 499 549.25; 520 17,116.55; 529 74,431.79; 530 78,115.93; 700 444,178.30; 701 1,104.74; 750 27,863.44. Larger items include Hoekstra Transportation school buses $1,747,566.00, Apple Computer $329,088.00 and T M P Architecture $218,482.19 in fund 414; First Group America $231,845.37 for general education and $210,600.72 for special education transportation; Advanced Placement testing $137,398.00 for Troy High and $83,107.00 for Athens; Enviro Clean Services $200,836.63; City of Troy $56,964.02; and Desert Angels Inc. $30,000.00 for Athens charity week.

**Personnel.** The Board accepted with appreciation the resignations of Kenneth Miller, Executive Director of Maintenance & Operations, hired April 1, 2002, effective October 6, 2014, and Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent of Business Services, hired July 1, 2010, effective September 26, 2014. Probationary hires for 2014-2015: Meredith Adkins, .5 FTE speech language pathologist, Services Building; Taylor Firman, 1.0 FTE social studies, Larson Middle and Troy High; Rebecca Johnson, .4 FTE social studies, Troy High; and Holly White, .8 FTE mathematics, Baker Middle School. Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources, reported the third year of the Troy Educator Appraisal Model and a move from STAGES to Teachscape: 574 teachers Highly Effective, 201 Effective, 9 Minimally Effective, 2 Ineffective; administrators 26 Highly Effective, 10 Effective, 1 Minimally Effective under a process newly based on Reeves' Leadership Performance Matrix. Absences for personal-family illness, bereavement or personal business fell from 7,790 in 2012/2013 to 6,112 in 2013/2014, a reduction of 1,678 absences. Of 447 teachers applying for Performance-Based Compensation, 416 received some portion — 262 at $1,256.28 (100%), 113 at $942.21 (75%) and 41 at $628.14 (50%) — for total PBC paid of $461,371.83 without TSD-paid FICA and retirement; the 2014/2015 model excludes up to four annual bereavement days.

**Curriculum.** The 2014/2015 Sex Education Advisory Board roster, updated 10-2-14, is co-chaired by Amy Buchanan, Assistant Principal at Smith Middle School, and parent Nicole Jenkins, with Rev. David Huseltine of Big Beaver United Methodist Church and nurse Lois Winer of the Oakland Health Department. Anne Mull presented 2014-2015 professional development, including an administrative retreat with Kathy Lassiter presenting the work of Vivian Robinson, quarterly peer district meetings hosted by TSD in October, and initiatives including job-embedded PD and Multi-Tiered System of Support. Mark Dziatczak reported 170 AP Scholars (average 3.28), 90 AP Scholars with Honor (3.71), 252 AP Scholars with Distinction (4.26) and 76 National AP Scholars (4.58); 2013-14 testing showed 2,745 exams, 1,176 testers and 2,248 scores above 3, or 81.90%; 2013 AP Equity and Excellence was 39.9% at Athens, 52.5% at Troy High and 46.7% districtwide.

**Business.** Bid 9796, per an October 1, 2014 memo from Purchasing Supervisor Todd Hensley (Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248.823.4091), sought a wireless web-based system monitoring temperatures in freezers, coolers, milk boxes, storerooms and dishwashers; five bidders were invited and two responded, reviewed with Sodexo manager Gayle Moran. The award, subject to Michigan Department of Education approval, went to SMART Temp, LLC at $38,504.00 from the 2014-15 Food Service Fund, against Great Lakes Hotel Supply at $41,637.00 and an alternate SMART 2013-software quote at $34,734.00. Dr. Richard Machesky was proposed as temporary Treasurer of the Troy Board of Education until an Assistant Superintendent of Business Services is appointed. Item 8.C awarded Athens High School addition and remodeling masonry to Efficient Design, Inc. at $73,482.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund; the October 6, 2014 memo notes the award is approximately $3,482 over the budgeted amount of $70,000, an unfavorable budget variance. A Barton Malow Company letter of October 2, 2014 from 26500 American Drive, Southfield, Michigan 48034 to Kenneth Miller states that Bid Package 4 contracts were awarded August 5, 2014, that no masonry bids came in then, and that three bids arrived September 18, 2014: Efficient Design $73,482.00, Silverado Construction $102,500.00 and NACE $112,600.00.

**Other.** Committee assignments for 2014/2015 place Philippart on Oakland Schools' Legislative Committee, Fleming on the Senior Advisory Committee and Troy Community Coalition, Miletti and Fleming on the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, Hauff on Troy Parks and Recreation, Schmidt on Troy Youth Assistance, and Edmunds on Troy Historical Society. Dr. Machesky's annual report restated the mission "to ensure learning for all members of the school community" and the state expectation that 85% of all students and student groups of 30 or more be proficient by 2021-2022, with Annual Measurable Objectives built from 2011-2012 proficiency. Accountability colors moved Niles Community High School from RED to YELLOW and Bemis, Boulan Park, Costello, Hamilton, Hill and Schroeder from LIME to YELLOW; the district scorecard was YELLOW. 2013-2014 MEAP reading proficiency was 83, 88, 90, 89, 85 and 88 percent for grades 3 through 8; mathematics 69, 79, 82, 82, 78 and 72; science, labeled 2012-2013, 25 at grade 5 and 29 at grade 8. AP course enrollment was 1,272 students, 36% of the student body, in 2012-2013 and 1,376, or 37%, in 2013-2014; dual enrollment was 27 and 41 students, not including OCALC. All TSD teachers are Highly Qualified, 69% hold a master's degree or higher and 7 have earned a Ph.D., Ed.D. or J.D. Goals for 2014-2015 covered operational effectiveness in business services and human resources, evaluation of privatized preventative maintenance crews and of bond implementation with TMP and Barton Malow, 85% successful completion of early college and career programs, a new web vendor for Fall 2015, a 90-Day Entry Plan report at the October workshop, and a decision-making matrix to be implemented January 2015. Item 10.C was a bond projects update requiring no action.
